'''Sir John Alexander David Aston {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}''' is a British statistician, Chief Scientific Adviser (CSA) at the Home Office (2018–2020), and
Professor of Statistics, Statistical Laboratory, [[University of Cambridge]]. From 2021 he is the Harding Professor of Statistics in Public Life.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2020-21/weekly/6595/6595.pdf|title=Elections|website=Cambridge University Reporter}}</ref> And from July 2021 he has also served as a non-executive director on the board of the [[UK Statistics Authority]].

Aston earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Cambridge, and a PhD in statistics from [[Imperial College London]] and [[McGill University]] in Montreal, Quebec.<ref name="NISS">{{cite web |title=John Aston |url=https://www.niss.org/people/john-aston |website=National Institute of Statistical Sciences |date=8 July 2015 |accessdate=25 April 2020}}</ref> He was an academic at the [[University of Warwick]] and at [[Academia Sinica]] in Taiwan, before becoming a professor at the University of Cambridge.<ref name="CSaP">{{cite web |title=Professor John Aston |url=http://www.csap.cam.ac.uk/network/john-aston/ |website=Centre for Science and Policy. |accessdate=25 April 2020}}</ref>

Aston was one of the 23 attendees of the [[Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies]] (Sage) during the early stage of the SARS-CoV2 pandemic owing to his CSA role at the time.<ref name="The Guardian">{{cite news |last1=Sample |first1=Ian |title=Who's who on secret scientific group advising UK government? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/apr/24/coronavirus-whos-who-on-secret-scientific-group-advising-uk-government-sage |accessdate=24 April 2020 |work=The Guardian |date=24 April 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He and his wife, Karri, have three children.<ref name="NISS"/>

==Honours==
He was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2021 Birthday Honours]] for services to statistics and public policymaking.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63377|supp=y|page=B2|date=12 June 2021}}</ref>
